title: Introduction to neural networks
description: A sample course written by Adle. It follows one idea from a single neuron to backpropagation: how a network of simple units learns from its mistakes. Nothing in it comes from your own materials.

concepts.title: Weights and bias
concepts.summary: How a neuron combines its inputs into a single number: multiply each input by a weight, add the results, and add a bias.

objectives.statement: Compute a neuron's weighted sum, including the bias, by hand.
Say what a large, small, zero, or negative weight means for an input.
Explain what the bias changes that the weights cannot.

concepts.title: Activation functions
concepts.summary: The function a neuron applies to its weighted sum, and why a network needs one that is not a straight line.

objectives.statement: Apply a step, sigmoid, or ReLU function to a given value.
Explain why a network without activation functions can only draw straight lines.
Describe how sigmoid and ReLU differ for large negative and large positive inputs.

needs.reason: An activation function is applied to the weighted sum.

concepts.title: The perceptron
concepts.summary: A single neuron used to make a yes-or-no decision, and the boundary it draws between the two answers.

objectives.statement: Decide which answer a perceptron gives for a given input.
Describe the decision boundary of a perceptron with two inputs, and how the weights and bias move it.
Give an example of a problem a single perceptron cannot solve, and say why.

needs.reason: A perceptron starts by computing a weighted sum.
Its yes-or-no answer comes from a step activation.

concepts.title: Forward propagation
concepts.summary: How an input travels through the layers of a network, each layer's outputs becoming the next layer's inputs.

objectives.statement: Compute the output of a small two-layer network by hand.
Explain what a hidden layer is and why its outputs are not seen directly.

needs.reason: A network is built from neurons like the perceptron.
Every layer applies an activation function.

concepts.title: Loss
concepts.summary: A single number that says how wrong the network's predictions are, so that "better" has a meaning.

objectives.statement: Compute a mean squared error for a few predictions and targets.
Explain why errors are squared before they are averaged.

needs.reason: The loss compares the network's output with the target.

concepts.title: Derivatives and the chain rule
concepts.summary: How fast one quantity changes when another does, and how to find that rate through a chain of steps.

objectives.statement: Interpret a derivative as a slope: the change in output for a small change in input.
Use the chain rule to differentiate a function of a function.

concepts.title: Gradient descent
concepts.summary: Improving the weights step by step, by moving each one a little in the direction that lowers the loss.

objectives.statement: Carry out one gradient descent update for a weight.
Predict what happens when the learning rate is too small or too large.

needs.reason: Gradient descent exists to lower the loss.
The direction of each step comes from a derivative.

concepts.title: Backpropagation
concepts.summary: Finding how the loss depends on every weight in the network by applying the chain rule backwards, layer by layer.

objectives.statement: Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to a weight in a small network.
Explain why working backwards from the loss saves repeated work.

needs.reason: Backpropagation retraces the forward pass in reverse.
It is the chain rule applied layer by layer.
It supplies the gradients that gradient descent uses.
